content:
ashley_support: heads up — Acme says their June invoice is ~7.2M tokens but dashboard shows ~2.1M. They suspect streaming disconnects + client-side cancels caused double-counting. request_id: r-0a9f1234. attaching snippets below.

acme_engineering: we had flaky mobile connectivity. lots of streams aborted mid-generation, then clients reconnected and resumed. we only render final message to users, so invoice surprise. example session id: s-78b2. attached our client log lines.

leo_client: can you paste the server-side event trace for r-0a9f1234? want to see event ordering.

jordan_sre: pulling metering logs now. quick theory: when client cancels mid-chunk runtime emits a partial token event, then on reconnect a new session_id is created and counts from resumed tokens are billed separately. dedupe usually uses `stream_id` but I see gaps in the header in these traces.

acme_engineering: sample client sequence we see: connect -> start generation -> network blip -> client abort -> immediate reconnect -> resume. we never sent an explicit finalize.

jordan_sre: server trace (sanitized):
```
[2028-06-12T15:22:03Z] r-0a9f1234 session=s-78b2 stream_id=none event=generate_chunk tokens=412
[2028-06-12T15:22:03Z] r-0a9f1234 session=s-78b2 event=client_cancel
[2028-06-12T15:22:04Z] r-0a9f1234 session=s-78b3 stream_id=null event=connect tokens=0
[2028-06-12T15:22:05Z] r-0a9f1234 session=s-78b3 stream_id=null event=generate_chunk tokens=398
```
Notice stream_id is null on reconnect — that prevents the metering service from collapsing events into one stream.

sam_billing: pulled invoice lines for account a-456: invoice 2028-06 line_item token_count=7231456, dashboard_total=2187201. we need an audit trail (list of token_events and their session/stream ids) before issuing credit.

jordan_sre: here's the query I used to compute per-session tokens (internal):
```
SELECT session_id, stream_id, SUM(tokens) as total_tokens
FROM token_events
WHERE request_id = 'r-0a9f1234'
GROUP BY session_id, stream_id;
```
Output shows two session rows with similar token totals.

invoice-bot: billing-run br-20280601-5 processed at 2028-06-01T00:00:00Z. All unadjusted token_events were imported into invoice lines.

jordan_sre: root cause appears to be streaming-router race: when TCP resets happen, we create a fresh session and don't carry forward `stream_id` when reconnect comes within <5s. metering uses `stream_id` to dedupe partials. fix path: persist a client-supplied `X-Stream-Fingerprint` header and prefer that to ephemeral session ids.

ashley_support: customer is asking for credit and immediate mitigation. can we produce a list of affected invoice_line_ids and per-session evidence for Sam?

sam_billing: will provision provisional credit once we have the CSV of affected invoices + evidence. please include: invoice_id, line_item_id, token_events (ids), and a short explanation.

leo_client: eng will ship a hotfix that requires library to send `X-Stream-Fingerprint` or fall back to session cookie. hotfix ETA: 3h to canary, 24h to full rollout. short-term: we can run a dedupe pass for br-20280601-5 where we collapse token_events that share request_id and close timestamps within 10s and lack stream_id.

acme_engineering: we'll gather client logs and give you reconnect patterns. thanks for quick response.

jordan_sre: repro steps I used locally to trigger double-counting:
1) start streaming request with header `X-Stream-Fingerprint: repro-uuid-1234`
2) while server is mid-generation, send `tcpkill -i lo port 443` (simulate network drop)
3) client reconnects immediately with same fingerprint but runtime previously returned null stream_id -> new session created -> two token_events billed

mini repro curl (simplified):
```
# start (server produces a long stream)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Stream-Fingerprint: repro-uuid-1234" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-xyz
# kill connection after ~2s then restart
```

ashley_support: i'll update Acme and mark this P1 for billing ops + eng. Sam will coordinate the provisional credit and jordan will post a postmortem + final reconciliation once we have the dedupe run results. :thumbsup:

sam_billing: noted. assigning ticket BILL-1429. I'll follow up in this thread with CSV by EOD.
